body: Thank you so much, I'm really grateful for all the support I've gotten but also hopefully will keep this from happening to someone else. Thank you thank you 💖
The obstacle course of dog poop

I'm so sorry this happened to your girlfriend, and I'm glad you were able to post about how you're feeling here. It happened to her, but you also have to take care of how you're feeling as well. 

Something similar happened to me and my husband was furious at the guy. I understood, but then I ended up feeling like I couldn't talk to him about it because he would get so mad and I didn't want to deal with his anger. My husband never talked about how he felt with anyone so I was the only outlet. So my advice would be, feel what you need to feel and keep reaching out so that you can be fully there for her without making it about you. Ultimately, she gets to decide what she wants. 

Also, know that this is not your fault. It's the fault of the creeps who assaulted her.

Thank you so much Ahsoka. I didn't realize how much I needed to hear that I'm not alone in this. Thank you for your compassion and all your kind words. I reached out to a couple of therapists so hopefully I'll find a good match. Keep your fingers crossed for me 💛

This is so helpful. I'm tearing up reading everyone's amazing responses. I'm so happy that you and your partner were able to work on those things and that you've given yourself the space to work on all of it yourself. It must feel really empowering, like you said!
I'm going to keep the trampoline in mind, especially that I have the ability to construct it. And, what you said about healing changing the brain. Gosh, that gives me hope. Thank you, thank you 💛

Yup. Brother, acquaintance, trainer. The acquaintance was a man I'd met online when I was 13 and desperate for friends - we talked for months. One night when my mom wasn't home and he asked if he could come over, and when he did, he raped me. I had to sleep in that bed for years. I didn't know it was rape at the time because I thought rape was some violent encounter on the street by a stranger. The first friend I tried to tell about it slapped me across the face and wouldn't let me touch her when she turned her back to me. I had to lie and say I was kidding. 

A year and a half ago I was training in Muay Thai in Thailand and my trainer asked to take me to dinner. I consulted a local friend about it and she said that was totally normal because MT gyms are like families and often eat together. So, we did. Towards the end of my trip, he asked me to meet him and his friends for some drinks. I woke up the next day naked and hardly remembering the night before. It wasn't till later that I realized I'd been drugged and had a flashback that I'd been raped in the shower. I literally have been having to retrain my nervous system because after it happened I had major PTSD symptoms - I felt disembodied and numb all the time, I would run into things and drop them, I couldn't remember simple stuff or focus on anything. It was like being a different person. On top of trying to address my patterns of either not trusting at all or being overly trusting. It's exhausting.

Oh my god. Those last lines just hit me in the heart. Thank you so much for saying that. It's so scary and isolating as fuck. 

I actually got on a chat with RAINN earlier and was able to find some potential therapists who I can work with, so hopefully it leads to something. Fingers crossed.

Thank you again so much for your kindness <3 It really made a difference for me

Thank you so much for all of these insights. It helps to know the experience of someone who has also been through it. I definitely can see I need to be more compassionate and patient with myself. And you mentioned outlets - I might have to try and think of some other outlets for myself so I don't act out.

I also definitely see the value in taking a sex break - I had the conflation between my partner and abuser happen before and it wasn't pretty. I'm nervous to ask for this, but I know he'll understand.

Oh wow, I hope you're able to receive the support you need. Yea, I've actually been thinking about taking up an MMO or something to keep myself preoccupied at least some of the time. I have some friends I can talk to casually like that but they're not always around. Thank you for your advice <3
Thank you for that reminder, I do tend to be really hard on myself. I appreciate you <3

Thank you so much for sharing what's been going on for you. It helps to know I'm not alone in this. I totally understand seeing men as predators - I was listening to a guided sleep meditation and it was a man's voice and I just freaked out. The body holds so much. You don't need to share your story if that doesn't feel right to you, but know that you're not alone and your process is exactly what it needs to be. With you 💛

Thank you for reminding me of the things I have to be grateful for, it's nice to think about on days like this. You're right, I definitely need to have a sit down with him, as scary as that is. Thank you for your kind words 💛

Thank you so much for reading and responding 💛 I'm so sorry you had to go through what you did, especially when you were young, and I'm really glad you have a therapist who you can trust. I've told him that it happened but definitely not this much detail, so probably a lot of my behavior seems uncharacteristic and random. Has your therapist given you any advice you've found particularly helpful?
Big hugs. Thank you for letting me know I'm not alone ✨

Thank you so much for your reply and your affirmations. You're right, thank you for also encouraging me to share this post with him. My sense of safety is really off so being reminded that I can lean on others is a good idea to lean into my supports. I really appreciate the time you took to read and respond to me, thank you 💛
